explanation: Tipping is not a traditional Thai custom and is never strictly expected, especially at street food stalls and local eateries where rounding up is enough. In tourist-oriented restaurants and upscale venues a service charge (often around 10%) is commonly already added to the bill, and where it isn't, leaving 5-10% for good service has become a common, welcomed gesture. Skipping a tip entirely is not seen as rude by most Thai staff.
local_tip: Check the bill for an already-added service charge before tipping extra, and if there isn't one, leave loose change or round up in cash for good service.
regional_note: Tipping is far more common in tourist hubs and hotels in Bangkok, Phuket, and Pattaya than at small local or rural eateries, where it can still seem unfamiliar.

also_check.note: Tipping is not customary and can confuse or embarrass staff, since good service is assumed rather than purchased.
Tipping 15-20% at restaurants is standard and expected; leaving nothing is seen as a serious insult.
A service charge is included by law, so only a small amount of extra change for great service is needed.
